messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: alert — tenant crescent-financial (vpc:crescent-prod, dedicated-pool 7) elevated 5xx rate + increased tail latency at 2026-07-18T12:03:00Z. auto-pager: @oncall-ryan

oncall-ryan: seeing it, joining. can someone post early impact?

sre-sasha: I have dashboards up — errors are primarily model-inference 502/503 from the dedicated pool serving model 'redwood-rlhf-3b-v2' pinned for that tenant. error spike correlates with long prefix batches. latency median -> 320ms -> 1.8s. 90p -> 4.5s.

eng-ml-raj: hmm, that model variant had a recent kernel swap yesterday (quant-kernel-3). Could be memory pressure/regression with long KV cache. pulling logs now.

pm-emma: cs reports 4 customers complaining via support, one escalated to legal about degraded SLAs. Need ETA for mitigation.

cs-lina: confirmed — Crescent Financial is on Strict SLA. They see timeouts on critical payment flow. They want status and rollback plan.

eng-ml-raj: log snippet from runner: ```
2026-07-18T12:02:57Z runner[host-7]: kv_cache_alloc failed: OOM when reserving 512MB
2026-07-18T12:02:58Z runtime: fallback error -> variant_fallback() -> downstream 502
```

eng-ml-raj: looks like we hit per-instance memory ceiling under certain long-context requests. The dedicated pool isolation means other tenants unaffected.

oncall-ryan: steps I can do now: (1) temporarily pin Crescent to a safe-variant (redwood-rlhf-3b-v2-safe) that uses smaller KV memory / quant profile, (2) scale pool 7 by +2 instances, (3) enable aggressive prefix-trimming for that tenant. Which do we want first?

sre-sasha: pin + prefix-trim first. scaling is slower and might not help if kernel regression causes OOMs.

eng-ml-raj: agree. I can trigger safe-variant pin via the routing-api: ```curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/tenants/crescent/routing -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' -d '{"pin": "redwood-rlhf-3b-v2-safe", "reason": "runtime OOMs - emergency safe variant", "ttl": 3600}'```

oncall-ryan: doing it now.

incident-bot: action acknowledged — routing change job queued (job-id: rjob-87321). Notifying telemetry.

oncall-ryan: rjob-87321 -> succeeded. pinned to redwood-rlhf-3b-v2-safe. Applying tenant-level prefix trimming policy: trim_prefix=true, max_prefix_tokens=1024.

eng-ml-raj: can confirm runner logs show fewer OOMs post-pin. sample: ```
2026-07-18T12:05:40Z runner[host-7]: model redwood-rlhf-3b-v2-safe loaded, kv_limit=384MB
2026-07-18T12:05:45Z runtime: request ok, latency 420ms
```

sre-sasha: metrics: 5xx rate for crescent-financial dropped from 14% -> 1.7% over 90s. tail latency down.

cs-lina: relaying to customer — they're seeing improvements. asking for ETA on permanent fix and rollback policy.

pm-emma: short answer: we'll keep safe-variant pinned and continue investigation. proposal: keep pin for 12h while eng-ml runs kernel regression and a controlled rollback on a canary host. If regression cleared, we can unpin and do gradual canary. Anyone object?

eng-ml-raj: fine. I'll repro locally against quant-kernel-3 with long prefix tests and try revert to quant-kernel-2 on a canary host. If revert stabilizes, we'll schedule canary revert in dedicated pool 7 with traffic cutover 5% -> 25% -> 100%.

oncall-ryan: creating incident ticket INC-2026-0743, paging rotation updated: primary oncall -> ryan, followup -> sasha.

incident-bot: incident INC-2026-0743 created. severity: P1 (customer-impacting, enterprise SLA). Pager duty runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/INC-2026-0743

eng-ml-raj: quick note on rollback safety — because tenant was pinned at routing layer, unpin will route them back to the pool default model. We'll only unpin after canary pass and after adding a memory-safe kernel flag to autoscaler config.

pm-emma: I'll own customer comms updates (every 30 minutes) and legal/system status. cs-lina will manage direct customer updates.

cs-lina: update sent: "We have applied a temporary safe model variant and observe restored service. We are working on a targeted kernel rollback and will update within 1h."

sre-sasha: followups for postmortem: root-cause analysis of quant-kernel-3 memory accounting, add tenant-level early-trim heuristics, add circuit-breaker on per-runner memory spike, add dashboard alert to correlate kv_cache_alloc failures.

eng-ml-raj: logging note — add more context to runner OOM logs (tenant, model-version, kv_usage) before closing.

oncall-ryan: passing to night team in 45m. if escalations come up, page me.

pm-emma: thanks all. I'll file the post-incident action items and schedule a war room with eng-ml and sre in 2h. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated (service restored for tenant). Monitoring for 30m.

cs-lina: customer acknowledges improvement and holding on additional verifications. No SLA credit request at this moment.

sre-sasha: leaving notes in ticket: mitigation = safe-variant pin, prefix trim, pending kernel rollback canary.

eng-ml-raj: will post PR with test vectors and kernel revert plan in the canary branch (link to follow).

oncall-ryan: closing here for now, we'll reopen if regressions reappear.
